label: Ashvale Dry Lake, symptom 'drive_grease_degradation'
headline: Ashvale's 9x drive-grease rate is an artifact of one technician's templated write-ups and inconsistent resolution coding — the same failure appears at four other sites and should be investigated as a drive-vintage cohort, not an Ashvale problem.
action: Re-cut this analysis by tracker drive vintage/serial cohort across all sites rather than by site, and correct Ashvale's symptom and resolution coding (author-templated narratives and resolution_code/action mismatches) before any site-level rate is used again.
reasoning: The matched controls kill the site-specificity claim: the exact same failure mode, with near-identical wording, appears at Dry Creek Junction (WO-2024-00073, WO-2025-00535), Tallow Branch (WO-2025-01161) and Red Clay Flats (WO-2025-00728), where techs explicitly call it 'normal wear for the vintage' and 'the fourth one this quarter' — so drive grease hardening is a fleet-wide, cross-site phenomenon, not an Ashvale environmental or lot effect (defeating H1 and H2). Within the cluster, three narratives are byte-identical templates from a single author, TECH-0194 (WO-2024-00061, WO-2024-00274, WO-2025-01170), and 5 of 8 members come from that one tech, which is the mechanism H3 predicts for an inflated site-level symptom rate. Coding reliability at Ashvale is demonstrably poor — WO-2024-00125 is resolution_code NO-FAULT-FOUND on a drive replacement, WO-2024-00274 is PART-REPL with no parts and a clean-and-repack narrative, WO-2024-00318 is ADJUSTED with a gearbox consumed — so the symptom label cannot be trusted to separate Ashvale from peer sites. Severity also argues against material impact per H4: most events resolve by regreasing at 2–7 labor hours, WO-2025-00505 explicitly reports backlash still within spec, and total lost generation across the eight events is 4.5 MWh on a 3.6 GW-month denominator. The honest read is that Ashvale is not distinguishable from the controls once labelling and author concentration are accounted for.
contradicting: Three Ashvale members show genuine hard failure rather than mere dry lube — scored gear faces and drive replacement in WO-2024-00125 and WO-2025-00297, and a gearbox consumed in WO-2024-00318 — and WO-2026-00052 independently describes grease 'dried out and gritty', consistent with abrasive ingress. The controls at Dry Creek Junction, Tallow Branch and Red Clay Flats also repeatedly attribute the same failure to a shared drive 'vintage', so a real fleet-level drive-lot problem may exist even though it is not Ashvale-specific; that belongs in a cohort-level candidate, not this site cell.

population_detail.description: Ashvale tracker population cannot be sized; installed_base is null and no per-block tracker counts were provided.

hypotheses.statement: A defective or under-specified grease/seal package on one lot of tracker slew drives — concentrated in blocks B04 and B06 at Ashvale Dry Lake — is drying out and hardening early, producing genuine drive-drive failures at ~9x fleet rate.
predictions: Affected asset_ids cluster in a subset of blocks (B04/B06 supply 6 of 8 here); a block-level breakdown of the site's full tracker population shows drive WOs disproportionate to trackers installed per block.

Narratives should repeatedly report irreversible damage, not just dry lube: 'gear faces scored', 'backlash out of spec', and parts_used='gearbox'/drive replacement in a substantial fraction (2 of 8 sampled already show this).
Repeat WOs on the same asset_id, or on adjacent row numbers (R090/R095/R096), should appear within 12-24 months with recurrence flags true.
Other Ashvale symptoms on non-drive components (inverter, combiner, module) should NOT be elevated versus fleet — the excess is component-specific.
If commissioning/install dates are available, affected assets share a narrow install window or drive vendor/serial band.
discriminating_evidence: Per-block normalisation: strong concentration in B04/B06 with near-zero rate in other blocks favours a lot defect; uniform spread across all blocks favours the environmental hypothesis H2.
Presence of hard-failure evidence (scored gears, gearbox parts consumed, replacement rather than repack) separates a true defect from a mere lubrication-service backlog (H4).
Recurrence on the same asset after a clean-and-repack indicates the failure mechanism persists; one-and-done fixes argue against a defective drive lot.

hypotheses.statement: Ashvale's dry-lakebed setting drives abrasive alkali dust into drive housings, degrading grease site-wide — an expected site-environment effect rather than an equipment defect, and one that should be managed by a shortened relube interval.
predictions: Affected trackers are spread across most blocks and row numbers rather than clustered in one install lot.

Narratives contain abrasion/contamination language ('gritty', 'dried out', 'contaminated', 'dust') at a higher rate than the same symptom at other sites; at least one sampled WO already says 'dried out and gritty'.
Ashvale should also show elevated rates for other dust-mediated symptoms (module soiling, bearing/bushing wear, seal or actuator contamination) relative to fleet, not just drive grease.
Event dates should skew toward the dry/windy season or follow high-wind periods; the sample spans Jul/Aug/Nov/Apr/Jun/Nov/Jan, so a seasonality test is directly checkable.
Any other site in the corpus with a similar arid descriptor/geography should show a comparable drive_grease_degradation rate.
discriminating_evidence: Cross-site comparison: if two or three other arid sites also run well above the 0.24/GW-month fleet rate, environment beats a site-specific defect.
Co-elevation of unrelated dust-sensitive symptoms at Ashvale points to environment; isolated drive-only elevation points to H1.
Environment field is 'none_mentioned' in 8 of 8 extractions — if raw narratives at Ashvale mention dust far more often than the extractor captured, that also implicates extraction quality (H3).

hypotheses.statement: The cluster is largely a labelling/reporting artifact: one technician (TECH-0194, 5 of 8 WOs) writes a fixed template phrase for any noisy drive, so ordinary drive complaints at Ashvale get coded 'drive_grease_degradation' while equivalent events elsewhere land under other symptom labels.
predictions: Three narratives are byte-identical ('squealing, grease separated, cleaned and repacked') and two more are near-identical ('drive replaced. Grease hardened, gear faces scored') — a corpus-wide duplicate-string search should show these templates confined to a small set of tech IDs.
Author concentration: TECH-0194's share of this symptom greatly exceeds their share of Ashvale WOs overall; removing that author drops the site rate toward fleet baseline.

Other sites should show a compensating excess of adjacent symptom codes (drive_noise, tracker_binding, motor_fault) so that total drive-related WO rate per GW-month is similar across sites even though grease-specific rate is not.

Resolution_code and extracted action already disagree in at least 4 of 8 records (CLEANED with 'drive replaced'; NO-FAULT-FOUND with a replacement; PART-REPL with 'cleaned and repacked'), indicating unreliable coding at this site.
discriminating_evidence: Roll up to component level: if Ashvale's tracker_drive WO rate per GW-month is near fleet while only the symptom split differs, the cluster is a labelling artifact, not a real failure excess.
Author-stratified rates: if TECH-0231 and TECH-0187 at Ashvale report this symptom at fleet-typical rates while TECH-0194 is 10x, reporting culture dominates.

Physical corroboration — parts issued (gearbox/drive count from inventory), SCADA tracker-stow/position faults, or lost_mwh — would be present for real failures and absent for template-driven reports; note lost_mwh here is only 4.5 MWh across 8 events.

hypotheses.statement: Eight events over ~19 months on a small installed base is ordinary variation plus expected lubrication-interval wear; the headline lift is inflated by a tiny 3.6 GW-month denominator and by relube work being written as corrective rather than preventive.
predictions: Poisson check against the fleet baseline: expected count is ~0.86, so 8 is nominally significant, but the confidence interval on 3.6 GW-month exposure is wide — several other small sites in the corpus should show similarly extreme lifts on some symptom purely by chance.

Most WOs resolve with clean-and-repack, low labor hours (median ~4 h, total only 36.3 h), no parts consumed in 6 of 8, and negligible lost_mwh (4.5 MWh total) — consistent with routine servicing, not failure.
The PM work-order stream at Ashvale should show few or no scheduled drive-lubrication PMs, i.e. the CM backlog is substituting for a missing PM task.
Events should be roughly uniform over calendar time (they are: 2024-07 through 2026-01) rather than bursting after a single trigger date.
Tracker age at Ashvale should be at or beyond the typical relube interval relative to younger fleet sites.
discriminating_evidence: A false-discovery sweep: count how many site x symptom cells with exposure under ~5 GW-months exceed lift 5. Many such cells means this candidate is selection noise.
If Ashvale has a scheduled drive-lube PM that is being executed on time and these are still occurring, the benign-wear explanation fails and H1/H2 gain.

Severity profile: absence of scored gears, replaced gearboxes, and material lost generation across the full 8-member set (not just the sample) supports benign servicing; their presence supports a real defect.
